messages:
gina: seeing intermittent 401 on streaming endpoint for AcmeCorp. customer reports: chunks stream for ~20s then 401, request-id: rq_9abf7c. sample curl I used below.

marco: can you paste the exact curl you ran (include -v and --raw if possible)? also please capture the x-request-id header from response. share region + model + time window.

gina: ```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams?model=gpt-4o-mini" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cookie: session=abcd1234; auth_cookie=efgh5678" \
  --no-buffer --http1.1
``` 
I attached the debug snippet (trace shows keep-alive then 401 after ~22s). request id in logs: rq_9abf7c

olivia: run with `--trace-ascii stream.trace` too, and `--raw -i` so we get chunk boundaries. also capture `curl --version` and OS. if you can reproduce, include the full trace.log.

gina: partial trace pasted:
```
> GET /v1/streams?model=gpt-4o-mini HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.inference
> Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
<data chunk1>
<data chunk2>
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-request-id: rq_9abf7c
< www-authenticate: Bearer realm="redwood", error="invalid_token"
```
looks like token became invalid mid-stream.

miguel: this matches a refresh race we've seen where cookie-based refresh runs concurrently and invalidates the bearer token. quick repro idea:
1) start long stream with current bearer token
2) trigger refresh (call token refresh endpoint) from another client after ~15s
3) watch for 401. 
To isolate: try running same curl but remove cookies (`-H "Cookie:"`) so refresh via cookie can't kick in. If 401 disappears -> it's cookie/refresh race.

support-bot: :clipboard: Support Repro Checklist:
- request-id(s): rq_9abf7c
- curl (with -v, --raw, --no-buffer, --trace-ascii)
- region: us-west-2
- model: gpt-4o-mini
- time window & approximate local clock
- attach debug bundle (logs + server-side trace)

gina: I'll run isolated tests and collect trace files. should I redact session cookie and sk- token before upload?

marco: yes redact secrets. replace with `<REDACTED_TOKEN>` and `<REDACTED_COOKIE>`. keep the request headers names & lengths. include curl version (e.g., "curl 7.79.1") and OS.

olivia: one more: if you suspect corporate proxy, run with `--noproxy '*'` or from a host outside corp network. proxy sometimes rewrites chunking headers.

gina: thanks all — will upload traces to the ticket when done and link here. :thumbsup:
